articles.title: A Tooth Reveals T. rex Ran Hot — Nearly as Warm as You
articles.summary: By measuring chemicals inside fossil teeth, UCLA scientists found that T. rex had a body temperature of about 97°F — almost the same as a human's. That supports the idea that the giant predator was warm-blooded and active, not a sluggish reptile.

articles.title: Killer Whales Are Literally Exploding Sunfish — Here's Why
articles.summary: New footage from the Gulf of California shows orcas ramming dead sunfish so hard the fish burst apart. Scientists think it may help feed young orcas — or it might just be play. One marine biologist called it 'the coolest thing I have ever seen.'

articles.title: Cat Pee Contains a Hidden Chemical 'ID Card,' Scientists Find
articles.summary: Researchers identified 13 unusual fatty acids in cat urine that vary from cat to cat but stay stable for the same animal. These compounds may act as a lasting chemical signature, helping cats recognize who left a scent mark — even months later.
